Contract:
**Port/Adapter/Service dependency graph — mandatory in `## Module Contracts`**, one level above the per-entity DbC prose: the individual Port/Adapter blocks below answer "what does each contract promise", this graph answers "who depends on whom, in which direction" — a relationship among ≥2 elements, so it is a picture, not a bullet list (`AX_INFOGRAPHIC_FIRST`, `formats/diagram-vocabulary.xml`). Nodes = every Port / Adapter / Service this module defines or consumes from a sibling; edges = `implements` (Adapter → Port) and `depends on` (Service → Port), arrows drawn in the dependency direction — toward the more stable side (Stable Dependencies principle: an Adapter depends on its Port, never the reverse). Placed directly under the one-line human summary, above the folded `` block:
```markdown OrderService ──depends on──▶ PaymentGatewayPort ◀──implements── StripeAdapter ```
**Floor, never nothing:** a module with zero Ports/Adapters (Services only, no confirmed variability) still states that explicitly — `Граф не рисуется: в модуле нет Port/Adapter, только Service ` — the reader sees the DECISION (no abstraction layer here) instead of wondering whether the graph was forgotten. A single Port with a single Adapter and no other module depending on it draws the minimal two-node arrow above; it still earns the picture because direction-of-dependency is exactly the fact a reader must not have to infer from prose.
This ASCII form is shown in chat during STEP_4_CONTRACTS_DBC, at the point Port-vs-Service is decided (`AX_CHAT_BEFORE_SPEC`); the mermaid `flowchart` version under `## Module Contracts` is the same shape converted at write time — never a fresh diagram invented then.
